provision_review.why: 199A(a) allows the deduction only to non-corporate taxpayers, and (i)(1) only re-sizes 'the deduction allowed under subsection (a)'. A corporation, which gets no (a) deduction, therefore cannot get the $400 floor. The pre-fix final rule returns max(before_minimum, minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount) for any applicable taxpayer with no corporation guard; the post-fix rule returns 0 for corporations.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The final rule took max(pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi, minimum_active_qbi_deduction_amount) whenever the taxpayer was an applicable taxpayer under 199A(i), so a corporation with at least $1,000 of active QBI still received the $400 floor even though 199A(a) allows the deduction only "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" (the corporation guard existed only on the intermediate pre-minimum rule).
triage.triage_notes: Provision read through the pinned corpus release: 199A(a) reads "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation, except as provided in subsection (i), there shall be allowed as a deduction...", and 199A(i)(1) only re-sizes "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)" to the greater of that amount or $400 for an applicable taxpayer (aggregate active QBI >= $1,000) -- so a corporation, which gets no subsection (a) deduction at all, cannot receive the floor. Pre-fix file line 266 shows the corporation guard present on pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi but absent from the final rule, and the companion test added in this same commit (qbid-corporation-cannot-receive-active-minimum, taxpayer_is_corporation: true, aggregate active QBI 1000) asserts final = '0' with before_minimum = '0', which is exactly the value that would have been $400 pre-fix. taxpayer_is_corporation was already a declared Boolean input pre-fix (no input/scope additions). Kind ambiguity worth a reviewer's eye: this is equally describable as unrepresented_clause (the 199A(a) "other than a corporation" carve-out missing from the final rule); I chose wrong_entity_or_scope because the commit subject and PR body frame it as an entity exclusion on the module's output surface ("corporation guard on the final (§199A(a))"). One quirk: the new condition proof atom with excerpt "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" was inserted into the atoms block of pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction (post lines 112-117), not into federal_qualified_business_income_deduction whose formula actually gained the guard; a later commit 598e55889 "fix: attach corporation proof to final QBID" moved it, so that follow-up is provenance-only (mechanical). No unrelated formula, parameter, version, or effective-date changes in this diff; PROGRESS.md was the only other file. PR #1004 has no reviews or review comments; its body covers the whole composition campaign, not just this commit.
triage.verifier_justification: The diff changes the final output rule's formula, wrapping it in `if taxpayer_is_corporation: 0`, so this is an encoded-meaning change, not bookkeeping. The pre-fix path was genuinely reachable and wrong: the imported gate `applicable_taxpayer_for_minimum_active_qbi_deduction` is defined in us/statutes/26/199A.yaml purely as `aggregate_qualified_business_income_from_active_qualified_trades_or_businesses >= active_qbi_minimum_threshold` with no corporation test, so a corporation with $1,000 of active QBI took `max(0, $400) = $400` even though the pinned corpus text of 199A(a) reads "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation ... there shall be allowed as a deduction", and 199A(i)(1) only re-sizes "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)". The module already declared the input `taxpayer_is_corporation` ("whether the taxpayer is a corporation and therefore outside section 199A(a)") and already guarded the intermediate `pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi`, so the final rule contradicted the module's own claimed scope rather than adding coverage it never claimed. The added companion fixture `qbid-corporation-cannot-receive-active-minimum` pins the $400 → $0 behavior change, and the defect is an entity-class scope error (the deduction reaching corporations), which fits wrong_entity_or_scope.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutation attempts that failed: (1) "the guard was already upstream" — false at the final rule; the corporation guard sat only on pipeline_qbi_deduction_before_minimum_active_qbi, and the 199A(i) floor branch bypassed it entirely. (2) "the imported applicable-taxpayer gate already excludes corporations" — false; us/statutes/26/199A.yaml line ~589 defines it solely as active QBI >= threshold. (3) "new coverage, not a defect" — false; `taxpayer_is_corporation` is an existing declared input and the rule's own `source:` says "26 USC 199A(a), (i)". (4) "mechanical" — false; the versions[0].formula body changed. Residual textual ambiguity, the only real counterargument: 199A(a) says "except as provided in subsection (i)", which a hostile reader could stretch to let (i) override the corporation exclusion; the natural reading is that (i) modifies only the lesser-of amount, since (i)(1) speaks of "the deduction allowed under subsection (a)" and no such deduction is allowed to a corporation. Alternate kind worth a reviewer's eye: unrepresented_clause also fits mechanically (the fix adds a source-stated carve-out), but the carve-out is an entity-class limitation, so wrong_entity_or_scope is the more specific label. Separate minor issue in the same commit, not affecting this verdict: the new proof atom with excerpt "In the case of a taxpayer other than a corporation" was inserted into the atoms list of `pipeline_trade_or_business_phasein_reduction` (diff hunk at pre-line 100-111), not into `federal_qualified_business_income_deduction`, whose atoms are unchanged in the post file — a misplaced provenance atom for the very guard being added.
